observations: A large face fills the frame against a black ground, with dark brown and shadow tones building the planes of the forehead, cheeks, and jaw, while one eye sits higher and more open than the other.

Loose looping lines in yellow, magenta, white, red, and cyan scatter across and beyond the face, many extending past the head's edge into the black surround, with several drip-like strokes running vertically down the cheek.

The mouth is open, showing teeth and red lips; a small artist mark sits in the lower-left corner; scrawled letterforms appear near the upper center of the face but read as marks rather than legible text.
reading: The face pushes close to the frame, its dark tonal mass anchored by a black ground, while loose colored lines refuse to stay inside the form. One eye holds steady; the other is half-lost in shadow. The open mouth and the vertical drips give the image a raw, unresolved feeling—neither fully composed nor fully falling apart. The colored loops read less as decoration than as pressure.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #133 and nnxyz nnotb #135. Those neighbors show strikingly different approaches—flat cyan silhouette versus dense layered marks on black—making #134's dark tonal face a distinct presence in the owned run.

connections.reason: Both works place a large face on a black ground with colored looping lines layered over dark tonal masses, and both show an open mouth with visible teeth—though the nifty-faces work tilts the head and multiplies the eye forms.

lookingQuestion: The two eyes sit at different heights and carry different amounts of shadow—what does that asymmetry do to where you look first and how long you stay there?
ambiguities: The scrawled letterforms near the upper center of the face may be text or purely gestural marks; they are treated here as marks only.
nnxyz nnotb #133 (flat silhouette on cyan) offers no useful formal connection to #134 beyond title adjacency and was omitted from connections.
